mainTopic: Whether moving to a new place (שינוי מקום) in the middle of eating or drinking requires a new ברכה, and how far that rule reaches
overview: This amud finishes רבי יוחנן's ruling that neither a change of wine (שינוי יין) nor a change of place (שינוי מקום) requires a new ברכה. The גמרא challenges him from a ברייתא that says a change of place does require a new ברכה, and it concludes that רבי יוחנן is refuted. רב חסדא, quoting רב הונא, then limits the ברייתא's rule to moving from one house to another. Moving between spots in the same house does not count. רב אידי בר אבין supports this from the ברייתא of רב הינק's school. The גמרא explains that רב הונא simply had not heard that ברייתא. רב חסדא adds a second limit of his own: the rule applies only to foods that do not need an after-ברכה in their place. For foods like bread, a person returns to his first meal, so no new ברכה is needed. רב ששת disagrees and says a new ברכה is needed either way. A ברייתא about a group that leaves to greet a חתן or כלה is then used to challenge רב חסדא. רב נחמן בר יצחק begins to answer, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רבי יוחנן's ruling: changing place needs no new blessing
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of רבי יוחנן's ruling: a change of place, like a change of wine, does not require a new ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי יוחנן said: Both a change of wine] and a change of place do not require a new blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last part of רבי יוחנן's ruling. He said that if a person moves to a different place while eating or drinking, he does not need to make a new ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the sentence, about switching wines, came at the end of the previous section. Here רבי יוחנן adds that moving locations does not break the eating either. In his view, the original ברכה still covers what you eat or drink in the new place.

keyTerms.meaning: A change of place: moving to a different location in the middle of eating or drinking
Must make a ברכה
And likewise; 'both this... and that...'

phrases.english: and likewise a change of place —
phrases.notes: This continues 'אחד שינוי יין' (a change of wine) on the previous amud.

phrases.english: does not require a new blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶחָד שִׁינּוּי מָקוֹם אֵין צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יוחנן's statement, which began earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, moving to a new place during eating does not require a new ברכה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says changing place does require a new ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that directly contradicts רבי יוחנן on changing place.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: A change of place requires a new blessing; a change of wine does not require a new blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן using a ברייתא. The ברייתא says moving to a new place does require a new ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees with רבי יוחנן about switching wines, since no new ברכה is needed. It disagrees with him about switching places. An אמורא like רבי יוחנן normally cannot argue with a ברייתא, so this is a serious problem for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A change of wine: switching to a different wine during the meal

phrases.english: They raised an objection: a change of place requires a new blessing,
phrases.notes: This is the quote from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: a change of wine does not require a new blessing.
phrases.notes: On this half, the ברייתא agrees with רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling stated in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a change of place needs no new ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא, which carries more authority than an אמורא, explicitly says a change of place does require a new ברכה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the challenge stands and רבי יוחנן's view on changing place is rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of רבי יוחנן is a conclusive refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives no answer to defend רבי יוחנן. It simply declares that he has been refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'תיובתא... תיובתא' means the question has no answer. From here on, the working rule is the ברייתא's: a change of place requires a new ברכה. The rest of the סוגיא now asks exactly when that rule applies.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation: a decisive challenge that cannot be answered

steps.whatToRemember: The accepted rule is the ברייתא's: שינוי מקום requires a new ברכה, while שינוי יין does not.

phrases.english: The refutation of Rabbi Yochanan is a conclusive refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from step 2 with no defense.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן is rejected. A change of place does require a new ברכה.

steps.title: רב הונא limits the rule to moving from one house to another
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting רב הונא, says the ברייתא's rule applies only when moving between houses, not between spots within one house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין was sitting before רב חסדא, and רב חסדא sat and said in the name of רב הונא: What you said, that a change of place requires a new ברכה, was only taught for moving from house to house. But from place to place within the same house, no new ברכה is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we accept the ברייתא, רב חסדא quotes רב הונא to narrow it. Only leaving one house for another counts as a change of place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'change of place' without defining it. רב הונא defines it: moving between houses breaks the eating, but moving within the same house does not. The rule stays in force; it just has a clearer border.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of...: a phrase that narrows a rule
From one house to another house
From one spot to another, here meaning within the same house
That which you said: a phrase that quotes an earlier rule in order to explain it

steps.confusionAlert: 'הא דאמרת' ('what you said') is not addressed to רב אידי personally. It is a standard way of quoting the earlier ruling, here the ברייתא. Also, 'מקום למקום' here means moving within the same house, not to any other location.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin was sitting before Rav Chisda,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָתֵיב רַב חִסְדָּא וְקָאָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: and Rav Chisda sat and said in the name of Rav Huna:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ שִׁינּוּי מָקוֹם צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ,
phrases.english: That which you said, that a change of place requires a new blessing,
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא from step 2.

phrases.english: they only taught it for moving from house to house;
but from place to place within the house, no.
phrases.notes: No new ברכה is needed in this case.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ שִׁינּוּי מָקוֹם צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מִבַּיִת לְבַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the accepted ברייתא and defines the scope of 'change of place'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only moving from one house to another counts as a change of place that requires a new ברכה. Moving within the same house does not.

steps.title: רב אידי supports רב הונא from the ברייתא of רב הינק's school
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין says that a ברייתא from the school of רב הינק (or בר הינק) teaches the same limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said to him: We learned this in the ברייתא of the school of רב הינק, and some say in the ברייתא of the school of בר הינק, just like you said.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידי tells רב חסדא that a ברייתא already supports רב הונא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The house-to-house limit is not just an אמורא's opinion. A תנאי source teaches it too, which gives it strong backing. The גמרא notes two versions of the school's name, רב הינק or בר הינק, but either way the ברייתא says the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we learned (in a תנאי source)
A ברייתא: a תנאי teaching outside the משנה
And some say: introduces another version of a name or text
Like you; in agreement with your view

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין:
phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי תְּנֵינָא לֵיהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא דְּבֵי רַב הֵינַק,
phrases.english: So we learned it in the baraita of the school of Rav Hinak,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא דְּבֵי בַּר הֵינַק כְּווֹתָיךְ.
phrases.english: and some say in the baraita of the school of bar Hinak, just like you.
phrases.notes: Whichever way the name is said, 'just like you' holds for both versions.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי תְּנֵינָא לֵיהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא דְּבֵי רַב הֵינַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 4 with a תנאי source.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's limit that only moving house to house requires a new ברכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the school of רב הינק (or בר הינק)

steps.title: Why would רב הונא just repeat a ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב הונא stated this as his own teaching if a ברייתא already says it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is רב הונא just teaching us a ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled. If the ruling is already in a ברייתא, what did רב הונא add by saying it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that an אמורא who makes a statement is adding something new. If his ruling is word-for-word a known ברייתא, his statement seems unnecessary. This is a challenge to the purpose of רב הונא's statement, not to its correctness.

keyTerms.meaning: He is teaching us; what new point does he come to make?
But then...?: introduces a puzzled challenge

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא רַב הוּנָא מַתְנִיתָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן?
phrases.english: But is Rav Huna merely teaching us a baraita?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא רַב הוּנָא מַתְנִיתָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the support from step 5 to question the need for step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב הונא's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a ברייתא already teaches it, an אמורא repeating it seems to add nothing.

steps.title: רב הונא had not heard the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב הונא reached the same ruling on his own, without knowing the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא had not heard the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers simply: רב הונא did not know this ברייתא existed, so he ruled on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His statement was not a needless repeat. It was his own independent reasoning, which happened to match the ברייתא. That match actually strengthens the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: He had not heard it

steps.whatToRemember: The house-to-house limit is supported both by רב הונא's own reasoning and by the ברייתא of רב הינק's school.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא מַתְנִיתָא לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Rav Huna had not heard the baraita.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא מַתְנִיתָא לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical: the speaker did not know the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא's statement seemed to add nothing beyond the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא ruled independently without knowing the ברייתא, so his statement was not pointless.

steps.title: רב חסדא's own limit: foods that don't need an after-blessing in their place
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, in his own name, begins a second limit: the change-of-place rule applies only to foods that do not require an after-ברכה in their original place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, רב חסדא sat and said in his own name: What you said, that a change of place requires a new blessing, we only said regarding foods that do not require a blessing after them in their place...
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a second limit to the change-of-place rule, this time in his own name. The statement continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's limit was about the type of move (house to house). רב חסדא's limit is about the type of food. The rule applies to foods that do not have to be followed by an after-ברכה in the same place, such as fruit or water. With these foods, leaving shows that the eating is over, so eating again later is a new start that needs a new ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: introduces an additional teaching
In his own name, not quoting a teacher
We only said this regarding...: a phrase that narrows a rule
Require an after-ברכה in their original place

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is unfinished. The contrast, foods that do require an after-ברכה in their place such as bread, comes next. Do not decide the full rule yet.

phrases.english: And furthermore, Rav Chisda sat
and said in his own name:
phrases.notes: Not quoting רב הונא this time.

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ שִׁינּוּי מָקוֹם צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ,
phrases.english: That which you said, that a change of place requires a new blessing,
phrases.notes: Again quoting the ברייתא in order to narrow it.

phrases.english: we only said it regarding foods
that do not require a blessing after them in their original place,
phrases.notes: Such as fruit or water. The sentence continues next.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ יָתֵיב רַב חִסְדָּא וְקָאָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate limit on the ברייתא's rule, alongside רב הונא's limit from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The change-of-place rule applies to foods that do not require an after-ברכה in their original place. The full contrast continues next.

steps.title: Foods that need an after-blessing in their place do not need a new blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא finishes his limit. For foods whose after-ברכה must be said where they were eaten, changing place does not require a new ברכה, because the person is returning to his original meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with foods that need a blessing after them in their own place, he does not need to make a new blessing. What is the reason? He goes back to his first, established meal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא completes the rule he began in step 8. He gives the other side of the rule and then its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some foods, like bread, have an after-ברכה that must be said in the place where they were eaten. So when the person leaves, he still has to come back to that spot to say ברכת המזון. His meal is still 'tied' to the first place, so eating somewhere else is just a continuation of that meal, and no new ברכה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: require a blessing
after them (an after-blessing)
in their own place, where they were eaten
what is the reason?
the first fixed (established) meal
he returns

steps.confusionAlert: 'Need an after-blessing in their place' does not just mean 'need an after-blessing.' It means foods whose after-ברכה must be said in the specific spot where they were eaten.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the idea of קביעות: a meal tied to a place stays alive even when the person walks away. The rest of the סוגיא tests this idea.

phrases.english: But items that require
a blessing after them in their place
phrases.notes: Foods like bread, whose after-blessing must be said where they were eaten.

phrases.english: he does not need to bless (again).
What is the reason?
He returns to the first established meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אבל דברים הטעונין ברכה לאחריהן במקומן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חסדא's second limit begun in step 8 and gives its reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Foods whose after-ברכה must be said in their place do not need a new ברכה after a change of place, because the eater returns to his original meal.

steps.title: רב ששת says a new blessing is always needed
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת disagrees with רב חסדא. For both kinds of food, a change of place requires a new ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said: Both this kind and that kind of food need a new blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא, רב ששת, disagrees with רב חסדא's limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא split the foods into two groups. רב ששת does not accept the split. In his view, changing place always breaks the meal, even for foods like bread, so a new ברכה is required either way.

keyTerms.meaning: both this and that (both cases are the same)
he needs to make a blessing

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said:
Both this and that,
he must make a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורב ששת אמר אחד זה ואחד זה צריך לברך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רב חסדא's limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Changing place requires a new ברכה for all foods, including those whose after-ברכה must be said in their place.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a group that leaves to greet a groom or bride
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב חסדא. A drinking group that leaves to greet a חתן or כלה needs no after-ברכה when leaving and no new ברכה when returning.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Members of a group were reclining to drink, and they got up to go out to greet a groom or a bride. When they leave, they do not need an after-blessing for what they ate. When they come back, they do not need a new opening blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a challenge by quoting a ברייתא. This step is setup: the challenge itself is built in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface, this ברייתא seems to fit רב חסדא's view, because leaving does not break the meal. But the ברייתא has a condition in its next line, and the גמרא will use that condition to attack.

keyTerms.meaning: members of a group eating together
reclining (sitting down to a meal)
they uprooted their feet (got up and left)
for what came before (an after-blessing)
from the start (a new opening blessing)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'למפרע' means the after-ברכה for what they already ate. 'לכתחלה' means the opening ברכה for what they will eat now. These are two different ברכות.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Members of a group who were reclining to drink,
and they uprooted their feet to go out
to greet a groom or to greet a bride,
when they go out,
they do not need a blessing for what came before (an after-blessing);
when they come back,
they do not need a new opening blessing.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: מימרא (quotation of the ברייתא as setup)
steps.triggerLanguage: מיתיבי בני חבורה שהיו מסובין לשתות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test רב חסדא's limit from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that foods needing an after-ברכה in their place need no new ברכה after a change of place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Still being built. The ברייתא's condition (next step) will show that leaving without someone remaining does require new ברכות.

steps.title: The condition: only if an old or sick person stayed behind
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits its rule. No new ברכות are needed only if an old or sick person was left at the meal. If no one stayed, they need an after-ברכה when leaving and a new ברכה when returning.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? When they left an old or sick person there. But if they did not leave any old or sick person there, then when they go out they need an after-blessing, and when they come back they need a new opening blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and adds a condition. The גמרא is still building its challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person who stays behind keeps the meal 'alive' in its place. Without him, the whole group's leaving ends the meal, so they must say the after-ברכה now and start over later. This second half of the ברייתא is what will clash with רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: in what case are these words said? (introduces a limit)
they left (someone) there
an old or sick person (who cannot go out)

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
When they left there an old or sick person;
but if they did not leave there
either an old person or a sick person,
when they go out,
they need a blessing for what came before (an after-blessing);
when they come back,
they need a new opening blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: במה דברים אמורים שהניחו שם זקן או חולה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא by adding its key condition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If nobody stays behind, the ברייתא requires new ברכות, even though the meal may have involved foods whose after-ברכה belongs in their place.

steps.title: The word 'uprooted' shows the case involves foods tied to their place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely. The word 'עקרו רגליהן' shows that the case involves foods whose after-ברכה must be said in their place. The only reason no new ברכות are needed is that an old or sick person stayed behind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the ברייתא says 'they uprooted their feet,' this shows we are dealing with foods that need a blessing after them in their place. And the reason they need no after-blessing when leaving and no new blessing when returning is only because they left an old or sick person there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the ברייתא's wording to set up the challenge against רב חסדא. The next step completes the attack with 'קשיא לרב חסדא'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Uprooting' suggests leaving a meal that is normally tied to its place, meaning foods like bread. So the ברייתא is talking about exactly the kind of food רב חסדא said needs no new ברכה. Yet the ברייתא says the ברכות are skipped only because someone stayed behind. That implies that without him, new ברכות would be needed, which goes against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: from the fact that it teaches (introduces an inference from wording)
by implication, this shows
we are dealing with

steps.confusionAlert: The proof comes from one word: 'עקרו רגליהן,' 'uprooted.' Watch how the גמרא builds a whole argument from the ברייתא's exact wording.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this inference holds, the ברייתא contradicts רב חסדא and supports רב ששת. The next part of the סוגיא must deal with this.

phrases.english: Since it teaches 'they uprooted their feet,'
this implies that with items that require
a blessing after them in their place we are dealing;

phrases.aramaic: וְטַעְמָא דְּהִנִּיחוּ שָׁם זָקֵן אוֹ חוֹלֶה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the wording of the ברייתא quoted in steps 11 and 12 to build the challenge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא deals with foods tied to their place and makes skipping the ברכות depend only on someone staying behind. This implies that without that person, new ברכות are required, against רב חסדא.

steps.title: If nobody stayed behind, new ברכות are needed, which challenges רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the ברייתא's second case: if no זקן or חולה stayed behind, the group needs a ברכה אחרונה when leaving and a new ברכה ראשונה when returning. This is a challenge to רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they did not leave an old or sick person there, then when they go out they need a ברכה for what they already ate, and when they come back they need a new opening ברכה. This is a difficulty for רב חסדא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ending of the ברייתא again, word for word. It uses that ending to finish its challenge against רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 showed that the ברייתא is about foods whose after-ברכה must be said in their place. רב חסדא said that for exactly these foods, changing place does not need a new ברכה. But the ברייתא says that when nobody stayed behind, leaving and returning DOES need new ברכות. So the ברייתא seems to contradict רב חסדא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge built in steps 11 to 13 by drawing the conclusion against רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling (step 9) that for foods whose after-ברכה must be said in their place, changing place does not require a new ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא is about those same foods (shown by עקרו רגליהן). Yet it says that when no one stays behind, leaving needs an after-ברכה and returning needs a new ברכה. That is the opposite of רב חסדא's rule.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק steps in to answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces רב נחמן בר יצחק, who will defend רב חסדא. His actual answer comes on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is only a setup. It tells us that רב נחמן בר יצחק is about to answer the challenge against רב חסדא, and his words continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a speaker's name is merged into his statement. Here this passage ends before his answer, so this line stands alone only as a bridge. Expect him to explain the ברייתא in a way that fits רב חסדא.
